sections.overview: The tomato leafminer is a small moth whose larvae damage tomato plants.
sections.identification: The larvae make conspicuous mines in leaves and can also bore into stems and fruit.
sections.habitat: It is closely associated with tomato crops, although other cultivated solanaceous plants can also be affected.
sections.diet: Larvae feed within plant tissues, especially tomato leaves and fruit.
sections.behavior: The larval stages remain concealed in mines or galleries, which can make early damage easy to overlook.
sections.reproduction: Its development is strongly affected by temperature, so generation time varies with conditions.
sections.ecology: EPPO currently uses the combination Phthorimaea absoluta, while Tuta absoluta remains widely used in agricultural sources.
sections.conservation: It is an agricultural pest rather than a species assessed here for wildlife conservation.
